text:
alex: Heads up — quarterly access scan flagged a cross-project KMS binding that looks like a privilege ripple. tagging eng-security :eyes:

maya: ugh. which role/key? paste the policy or audit slice pls

alex: role: infra-service-account@prod
bound to KMS key: projects/redwood-prod/locations/global/keyRings/payments/cryptoKeys/payments-key
policy shows a principal from project:analytics with `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter`

samir: that's a wide blast radius. can you dump the last 24h audit entries for SetIamPolicy on that key? i can run a quick query

alex: running now — here's the query i used:
```
resource.type="kms_key"
protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy"
resource.labels.key_ring_name="payments"
resource.labels.crypto_key_name="payments-key"
timestamp>="2026-03-22T00:00:00Z"
```
snippet: user: terraform@infra-team.project.iam.gserviceaccount.com performed SetIamPolicy at 2026-03-23T09:12:04Z

tess: also check the IAM policy history and the terraform plan. could be an unintended project-level binding from a TF module. `gcloud projects get-iam-policy analytics-project --format=json`

sec-bot: Alert created: INC-2026-42 Privilege ripple detected for KMS key payments-key. Pager duty: oncall. Links: /incidents/INC-2026-42

maya: i'll take triage. plan: snapshot binding, run policy simulator to see effective permissions, propose a scoped binding (if needed) and coordinate with payments eng. ETA ~2h

samir: while triaging, rotate any long-lived creds that might rely on that key (dataflow SA, etc). also surface any downstream services reading decrypted secrets.

tess: fyi infra PR 6523 touched that TF module this morning. @jon /infra-team — was that intended to add analytics as a consumer?

jon: yeah that PR added a migration job access to read encrypted blobs, but the binding accidentally used project-level principal instead of the job's service account. will open a revert/scope PR now

alex: reminder — need to avoid outage for payments. coordinate a canary removal first: remove analytics principal from one keyring, run smoke for payment flows.

maya: agreed. stepwise plan I'm executing:
1) snapshot current `get-iam-policy` and export to GCS
2) run IAM policy simulator for analytics principal to enumerate effective perms
3) patch TF to scope to `serviceAccount:migration-job@analytics.iam.gserviceaccount.com` instead of `project:analytics`
4) open revert PR and test in staging canary
5) rotate service account keys + rotate KMS key if we detect misuse

samir: add a loghook to alert on future `SetIamPolicy` for that key:
```
protoPayload.methodName="SetIamPolicy" AND
resource.labels.crypto_key_name="payments-key"
```
send to #eng-security with severity=high

tess: pinged payments-eng on the incident channel. asked for a quick signoff window for canary change

oncall: oncall here — can approve emergency revocation if payments sign off within 10m. otherwise i'll stand-by for manual rollback

jon: opened PR 6633 to scope binding. adding changelog and test plan. sorry — missed the scope in the module variable

alex: nice catch. can we also add a CI guard that prevents project-level KMS bindings in that module? simple policy check or tflint rule should do

maya: will add a one-off policy check in the repo and a longer-term policy-as-code RFC. triage update in ~90m.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-42 status: investigating -> mitigation in progress. assignee: maya

maya: quick update — simulator shows analytics lost `decrypt` after scoping to SA only. performed scoped canary on payments-staging, no failures. prepping prod patch and short maintenance window with payments team.

samir: rotated migration-job SA keys and created a short-lived key for the job. noted for postmortem: avoid project principals, prefer service accounts, and automate key rotation on role change.

maya: done: applied TF PR 6633 to prod (scoped binding), rotated SA creds, added the loghook alert, and archived the previous policy snapshot to GCS. opened RFC-priv-guardrails to add module linting. closing loop here — will add full postmortem to INC-2026-42

alex: thanks everyone. small follow-ups: add an alert runbook entry, and add a unit test to the TF module to catch `roles/cloudkms.*` at project level.

oncall: confirmed systems stable, payments signoff received. closing incident. :white_check_mark:
